ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated in the figure, within $ \triangle ABC$, D is the midpoint of AB. A line passing through D intersects AC at E and intersects the extension of BC at F. When $ BF=9$ and $ CF=4$, what is the value of $ \frac{AE}{EC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $CM\parallel AB$ through $C$, intersecting $DF$ at point $M$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle CME\sim \triangle ADE$, $\triangle FMC\sim \triangle FDB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{AD}{CM}$, $\frac{BD}{CM}=\frac{BF}{CF}$,\\
Moreover, $\because$ $AD=BD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{BF}{CF}$,\\
$\because$ $BF=9$, $CF=4$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EC}=\boxed{\frac{9}{4}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Construct $CM\parallel AB$ through $C$, intersecting $DF$ at point $M$,\\ $\therefore$ $\triangle CME\sim \triangle ADE$, $\triangle FMC\sim \triangle FDB$,\\ $\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{AD}{CM}$, $\frac{BD}{CM}=\frac{BF}{CF}$,\\ Moreover, $\because$ $AD=BD$,\\ $\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{BF}{CF}$,\\ $\because$ $BF=9$, $CF=4$,\\ $\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EC}=\boxed{\frac{9}{4}}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B, C, F are on the same horizontal straight line, and F is located to the right of C, that is, on the extension of BC. A is above, D is located on side AB, E is located on side AC; a straight line passes through D, E and continues to extend to F, therefore D, E, F are collinear. The problem gives that D is the midpoint of AB, so AD=DB, and BF=9, CF=4.

Reasoning: In triangle ABC, use Menelaus' theorem for the transversal line D-E-F. Since D is on AB, E is on AC, and F is on the extension of BC, the positive external division ratio form can be used:
(AD/DB)(BF/FC)(CE/EA)=1.
Because D is the midpoint of AB, AD/DB=1; also BF=9, FC=CF=4, so BF/FC=9/4.
Substituting gives: 1·(9/4)·(CE/EA)=1, therefore CE/EA=4/9.
So AE/EC=9/4.
